title: Bond order, bond length, and reaction heat estimates
objective: Relate bond order to length and strength and estimate reaction enthalpy from a bond inventory.

items.label: Bond enthalpy estimate
items.note: Multiply each bond energy by the number of those bonds.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Breaking absorbs energy; forming releases it. Count bonds per molecule and multiply by the coefficient. The bond-energy subtraction order differs from the formation-enthalpy method.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: Set up two labeled sums before calculating. Given a table, use the bond column matching the bond order.

blocks.title: Bond energy and reaction enthalpy
blocks.focus: Create a reactant and product bond inventory before substituting energies.

blocks.title: Hydrogen and chlorine
blocks.problem: Estimate $\Delta H$ for $\ce{H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2HCl(g)}$. Use 436, 243 and 431 kJ/mol for H–H, Cl–Cl and H–Cl.

steps.title: Break
steps.why: One reactant bond of each kind is dissociated.

steps.title: Form
steps.why: The coefficient produces two H–Cl bonds.

steps.title: Subtract
steps.why: More energy is released by formation than consumed by breaking.

blocks.title: Hydrogenate an alkene
blocks.problem: For $\ce{C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6}$, use C=C 614, H–H 436, C–C 347 and C–H 413 kJ/mol.

steps.title: Cancel common bonds
steps.md: Four C–H bonds occur on each side before counting the extra two in ethane.
steps.why: Matching bond types cancel in this approximate model.

steps.title: Count net changes
steps.md: Break one C=C and one H–H; form one C–C and two C–H.
steps.why: Treat the C=C as the full tabulated double bond.
